audit.why: EVEN 5.5/10 with Locke ahead at 6 and first item matches the 54.03% win rate over 385 games, and both layers agree row for row with the packet chart. No chart change.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every panel says 'when her W is down' and none of them said how long that is.
audit.why: Miasma is 24/22/20/18/16s — the longest cooldown in her kit and the entire step-up window for a champion whose only gap-close is a 10s blink. Twin Fang is 0.75s and Noxious Blast 3.5s, which is why the window has to be picked, not waited for.
audit.corrected: 24s at rank 1 stated in early and mid, the 0.75s Twin Fang in spikes[2] and spikes[3].

audit.whatIsWrong: Locke's Q was called Ritual Nails and his passive Silver Stake; Twin Fang's healing was never mentioned.
audit.why: Locke's Q is Soul Nails in his own kit text and the passive has no name in the file. Twin Fang heals Cassiopeia for a percentage of the damage dealt and refunds mana on a kill, so Grievous Wounds is live and her ramp is also sustain.
audit.corrected: Soul Nails used, passive described by its missing-health on-hit effect, Twin Fang's heal stated with the Grievous Wounds call.

audit.why: Miasma's grounding is the one mechanic that decides the lane and the page already states it plainly in breakdown.cooldowns, report[5], wants.you[0] and wants.foe[0]. The mirror flagged this as the gap on their side; on this side it was already correct.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are even but you have the edge in a fight: Cassiopeia's Q pokes yet her E needs a poison target, so when her W is down you can E in and out-trade her thin HP with Ritual Nails.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are even but you have the edge in a fight: Cassiopeia's Q pokes yet her E needs a poison target, so in the 24s her W is down you can E in and out-trade her thin HP with Soul Nails.

edits.before: Through 3-6 it stays skill-based — she wants to ground you with W and ramp Twin Fang while you dodge the grounding and use P Silver Stake to punish; managing her W cooldown decides the trade and your kit tilts it your way.
edits.after: Through 3-6 it stays skill-based — she wants to ground you with W and ramp Twin Fang while you dodge it and punish with missing-health on-hits; Miasma is 24s at rank 1 and 16s at max, and that window decides the trade.

edits.before: Cassiopeia pokes with Q Noxious Blast and lays E Twin Fang on her W Miasma poison; dodge her grounding W so she can't stop your E Ashen Pursuit, then close and trade with P Silver Stake.
edits.after: Cassiopeia pokes with Q Noxious Blast and lays E Twin Fang on her W Miasma poison; dodge the grounding so it cannot strand your E Ashen Pursuit, then close inside that 24s gap and bite.

edits.before: With her first item her Twin Fang DPS ramps hard if she keeps you poisoned, but you have kill pressure she lacks and your burst still beats her squishy frame.
edits.after: With her first item Twin Fang ramps hard while she keeps you poisoned, and it heals her off every tick — bring Grievous Wounds; your burst still beats her squishy frame.

edits.before: Cassiopeia becomes a grounding DPS turret; you must all-in through her W ground with E timing and burst her before Twin Fang stacks damage on you.
edits.after: Cassiopeia becomes a grounding DPS turret; step in only once Miasma is spent, and burst her thin frame before Twin Fang, up every 0.75s, ramps on you.

notes: This entry was already the cleanest in the slice — no fabricated enemy ability names and a chart that matches the packet. The only enemy-side gap was Twin Fang's healing, which makes anti-heal a real buy here; report[8] already says to add anti-heal, so the two now agree. 'Silver Stake' is not a name in Locke's kit file and was not reused.
